what_free: Free VPN with no bandwidth caps and no account required
Open-source client apps for Linux, macOS, Windows and Android
Run by a nonprofit activist collective - donations, not ads or tracking
best_for: A no-cost, no-signup VPN for basic traffic protection.
watch_out: Few exit locations; not built for streaming or strong anonymity

what_free: Free 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver plus WARP encrypted tunnel
No data caps; WARP+ optimized routing included at no charge
Apps for Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS and Android; malware-blocking Families mode free
what_paid: Zero Trust gateway policies, logging and organization management
best_for: One-tap encrypted DNS/VPN that protects traffic on hostile networks.
watch_out: Not an anonymity tool - Cloudflare terminates your traffic

what_free: Lightweight Windows firewall front-end over Windows Filtering Platform
Per-app allow/block lists plus a packet monitor
Portable single executable - no installation required
best_for: Controlling exactly which Windows apps reach the internet.
watch_out: Windows-only; rule model differs from classic firewall UX

what_free: Per-application network firewall and monitor for Windows and Linux
Default-block profiles, per-app DNS control and connection history
Fully open source; no account or subscription needed
what_paid: SPN adds multi-hop onion-style routing across Safing servers
best_for: Seeing and gating every app's network connections on your PC.
watch_out: Expect prompt fatigue while tuning rules at first

what_free: Full firewall/router OS: stateful filtering, traffic shaping, IDS/IPS (Suricata)
WireGuard, OpenVPN and IPsec VPNs with a clean web GUI
Regular releases; runs on x86 hardware and VMs
what_paid: Business edition adds professional support and extras
best_for: Turning spare hardware into a serious home or office firewall.
watch_out: Needs dedicated hardware; major upgrades occasionally need care

what_free: FreeBSD-based firewall/router Community Edition, free download
Firewall/NAT, OpenVPN/WireGuard/IPsec and package ecosystem (Suricata, pfBlockerNG)
Large community documentation and guides
what_paid: pfSense+ editions and hardware bundles with support
best_for: A long-proven BSD firewall distro with a big package ecosystem.
watch_out: CE updates lag; newest features live in pfSense+ on Netgate hardware

what_free: Replace vendor firmware on a long list of supported routers
Package feeds: WireGuard, SQM QoS, ad-blocking, VPN clients and more
LuCI web UI plus full SSH access
best_for: Unlocking real router features on consumer hardware.
watch_out: Flashing the wrong build can brick a router - check the device page first

what_free: Network-wide DNS ad/tracker blocking for every device on your LAN
Web dashboard with query logs and long-term statistics
Runs on Raspberry Pi, Docker or any small Linux box
best_for: Whole-household ad blocking without per-device apps.
watch_out: DNS-level blocking misses ads sharing a domain; occasional whitelisting needed

what_free: Self-hosted DNS server blocking ads and trackers network-wide
DoH/DoT/DoQ upstream support, per-client rules and parental controls
Single binary for routers, NAS, Docker or desktops with built-in web UI
best_for: Pi-hole-style blocking with easier setup and per-client controls.
watch_out: Filtering behavior differs slightly from Pi-hole

what_free: Lightweight Rust server compatible with official Bitwarden apps
Self-host unlimited users; includes attachments, TOTP authenticator and organizations
Single Docker container that runs on tiny hardware
best_for: A private Bitwarden-compatible password server on your own hardware.
watch_out: Third-party implementation - updates can trail the official server

what_free: Serverless messenger that syncs via Tor, Wi-Fi or Bluetooth
End-to-end encrypted chats, forums and blogs
Works even when the internet is censored or down; Android app plus desktop clients
best_for: Messaging that keeps working when networks are censored or down.
watch_out: No iOS app; delivery needs reachable peers (or Briar Mailbox)

what_free: End-to-end encrypted messaging with no user IDs, phone numbers or emails
Self-hostable relay servers; no central account registry
Apps for Android, iOS and desktop, plus a CLI client
best_for: Metadata-resistant chat without phone numbers or accounts.
watch_out: Younger ecosystem; contact onboarding works differently than mainstream apps

what_free: Search engine for internet-exposed devices and services
Free account with limited results and basic search filters
Handy for checking your own infrastructure's exposure
what_paid: More results per query, filters, export and API volume
best_for: OSINT recon on what your network exposes to the internet.
watch_out: Free tier heavily limits results; API access is metered

what_free: Amnesic live OS: boots from USB, leaves no trace on the machine
All traffic routed through Tor by default
Optional encrypted persistence; bundled Tor Browser and Thunderbird
best_for: Leave-no-trace, censorship-resistant computing from a USB stick.
watch_out: Tor speeds are slow; not a general daily-driver OS

what_free: Security desktop that isolates every app in its own lightweight VM
Separate qubes for work, personal, vault and disposable VMs
Free download with extensive documentation and community
best_for: Compartmentalized desktop for high-risk users like journalists.
watch_out: Demanding hardware: CPU virtualization extensions and generous RAM required

what_free: Modern file-encryption tool using X25519 keys or passphrases
Tiny spec and Go reference implementation; rage Rust port available
Great for encrypting files and backups for a recipient
best_for: Simple, modern file encryption without PGP complexity.
watch_out: Not OpenPGP - different key types and no web of trust

what_free: Full OpenPGP implementation: encrypt, sign and verify files and email
Key management, gpg-agent and smartcard support
Integrates with scripts, mail clients and CI signing workflows
best_for: Standards-based OpenPGP encryption and signing from the command line.
watch_out: Key management UX is notoriously beginner-unfriendly

what_free: Encrypted notes with cross-device sync on the free plan
Open-source apps for web, desktop and mobile
Local encryption before anything leaves your device
what_paid: More editors, themes and vault features
best_for: Simple encrypted long-term notes that stay out of the way.
watch_out: Free tier is deliberately basic; acquired by Proton (2024) so plans may shift

what_free: End-to-end encrypted notes with a rich editor and cross-device sync
Open-source apps for all platforms plus a web clipper
Notebooks, tags and favorites for organizing
what_paid: Pro unlocks extras like custom themes, larger uploads and advanced organizers
best_for: Feature-rich encrypted note-taking with a real free tier.
watch_out: Free plan has upload/space caps - check current limits

what_free: TOTP/HOTP two-factor token app
Fully offline - no accounts, no tracking
Android and iOS apps; FreeOTP+ fork adds export
best_for: A minimal open-source 2FA token app with no cloud involved.
watch_out: Official app lacks backup/export (FreeOTP+ fork adds it)

what_free: Android app for KeePass 2 (.kdbx) vaults
Opens databases from local storage or Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, SFTP, WebDAV
AutoFill/keyboard integration and full offline use
best_for: Android access to KeePass vaults across any storage backend.
watch_out: Functional rather than polished UI; cloud setup takes a step or two

what_free: Firefox-based browser with Tor Browser's anti-fingerprinting patches, minus the Tor network
Designed to blend in with other Mullvad Browser users
No account or VPN subscription required to use it
best_for: Fingerprint-resistant everyday browsing without Tor's speed cost.
watch_out: Traffic does not go through Tor - different model than Tor Browser
